- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model should not overreact — cap forecast slope at 0.5–1% per day to avoid overshoot.  
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.33), model should underpredict short-term volatility and allow for mean reversion toward 1–2% below forecast peak.  
- When 3+ consecutive auction events occur in 30d window, model should reduce forecast growth rate by 0.2–0.5% per event to reflect supply pressure.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model should not assume linear trend — apply smoothing or lagged correction to avoid false momentum.  
- For 30d forecasts with high negative supply net and low bullish sentiment, model should shift mean toward 1–2% below historical 30d average to reflect bearish bias.
